thread:
jamie: FYI — Payments team just hit the per-key limiter for their partner sandbox key. Ingestion dropped and they want a quick fix for a partner validation run. Do we want a temporary top-up flow or a different model for internal/service keys?

natalie: My preference is borrow from token-bucket semantics: keep per-key steady-state cap but allow a short burst window (eg 5x for 30s) with automatic cooldown. No manual forever-exceptions.

sahil: Agree on burst window, but also add an enforcement tier: per-org baseline + per-key burst ceiling + daily aggregate. That prevents sustained abuse while serving spikes. For internal services we can have a `service_role` flag that grants a one-time burst buffer that decays. Audit log every grant.

laura: UX note — Console should show live cap, burst remaining, and a single-click "request temporary top-up" that creates a ticket and expires automatically. Don't let people guess why requests failed. Also show which policy applied and a link to the audit entry.

mike: For partners we need SLA mapping (bronze/silver/gold) -> burst budgets. We can't just hand out internal exceptions to external partners. If Payments is a partner-facing flow, do this through partner-tier rules.

jamie: Good. Two practical questions: 1) how to store/annotate keys so runtime can decide fast (no DB hop on token path), 2) what should be the default auto-expire for a "temp top-up"?

natalie: Attach role and burst budget as immutable attributes in our key config entry replicated to cache (redis/local store) used by runtime. Temp-topups should be short: 5m default, configurable when requested, and must be echoed to audit and billing.

sahil: I'll prototype policy DSL for this. Rough sketch:
```json
{
  "policy": {
    "per_org_per_min": 1200,
    "per_key_burst_multiplier": 5,
    "burst_window_seconds": 30,
    "daily_max": 500000,
    "service_role_flags": ["internal_service", "partner_sandbox"]
  }
}
```
We can attach tags like `partner_sandbox` to keys; runtime uses a cached policy map.

laura: UX: when a temp-topup is issued we should label it "auto-expire: 5m" and show who requested/approved. If approved by automation, show automated reason + correlating deploy/incident id.

mike: Also need billing implications. If top-ups let partner blow past daily_max we have to either bill extra or deny. Prefer deny unless sales pre-approved.

jamie: Ops concern: any temp top-up flow must be kill-switchable and rate-limited itself (so someone can't spam requests). Also expose a safe fallback: route to a lower-cost model or cached responses when under pressure.

quota-bot: CurrentCounts: key=payments-sandbox-01 window=60s tokens_used=1180 limit=1200 burst_remaining=0

natalie: For rollout, gate behind a feature flag and only enable auto-topup for `internal_service` keys. Expand to partners after SLA and billing policy defined.

sahil: I'll open an RFC with the prototype DSL + runtime cache design + edge hook for console ticket flow. Targets: RFC by EOD Thursday, prototype in staging next sprint.

jamie: Perfect. If anyone has edge cases (webhooks, streaming) call them out in the RFC comments. :thumbsup:

mike: One more — streaming connections should be charged by concurrent slots not per-token burst. Add as separate rule in RFC.

laura: noted, will add UI mock for streaming slot view.

jamie: Thanks — I'll coordinate RFC reviewers (platform, payments, sales).
